_about: The life hub (plan 7.6f, third round). The words are the card's own and the family around them: the Hebrew חַי (חַיִּים, 'life', 'living', 'alive') and its verb חָיָה ('live', 'revive', 'keep alive'), the Aramaic חַי, חֶלֶד ('lifetime'), and the Greek ζωή, ζάω, ζῳοποιέω, ζῳογονέω, συζῳοποιέω and βίος; נֶפֶשׁ and ψυχή count only where the verse renders them 'life' (a life laid down, sought, lost), never where they are 'soul'. The frames carry the agent of only some of these verbs and no record of the participle ('the living God', 'living water'), so almost every row is made by hand where the text itself says what is meant (the divine persons by hand), and each pick was read against the Berean text. The contested points -- whether eternal life is had now, is still to come, or both; 'the righteous will live by faith' beside 'the man who does these things will live by them'; whether the dead of Ezek 37 and Rev 20:4-5 are raised in the body; whether a name written in the book of life can be blotted out; what the giving of a life does -- are set side by side, the text on each side, each with a note that the page takes no side. Built by tools/concepts/hub_build.py into out/concept-hubs/life.json.

titles.noun: What the text says of life

_words_why: The card lists נֶפֶשׁ (754 verses), חַי (497), ζωή, ψυχή, βίος, the Aramaic חַי and חֶלֶד. נֶפֶשׁ and ψυχή are 'soul' far more often than 'life', and the soul has its own card, so they enter only where MACULA glosses them 'life' (seek his life, lay down his life, lose his life, the life of the flesh); the sense rule does that (201 of the 683 verses of נֶפֶשׁ, 33 of the 92 of ψυχή). The card's 'other words' put חָיָה and ζῳοποιέω outside; they are the same family (the Greek Old Testament renders חָיָה by ζάω and ζῳοποιέω), so the hub takes them in with ζάω, which the card names under 'family', and ζῳογονέω and συζῳοποιέω ('made us alive together with Christ', Eph 2:5, Col 2:13). Hebrew, Aramaic and Greek are not said to be one word: every verse names the word it stands on. The Aramaic חַי shares its spelling with the Hebrew word, so it is listed first and the builder reads the clause words as Hebrew; its verses (Dan 4:34, 6:20, 6:26) are in the rows by hand.
_sense_why: Measured on MACULA's gloss in each verse (the card's occurrence list). חַי is glossed 'beast', 'animals', 'wild animals' (the living thing as an animal), 'raw' (raw flesh, Lev 13), 'fresh' (running water, Lev 14) and 'spring' (Gen 18:10, 'at this time next year'): those are other senses and drop (94 of the 447 verses). 'living' stays (the living God; every living thing), 'lives' stays (the oath 'as the LORD lives'), 'alive' stays. The Greek ζάω 'live' is matched the same way. The Hebrew 'living water' that the Berean prints 'fresh water' (Gen 26:19; Song 4:15) is left out of the water row, which shows only verses that say 'living'.

others._why: Other words the English also calls life, living or alive, named apart with their verses and never handed over as the same (as love names φιλέω): e.g. the Hebrew יוֹם 'day' where the Berean prints 'long life', Greek ζῷον 'living creature' (Rev 4), ἀναστροφή 'way of life', מִחְיָה 'sustenance'. The English 'live' as 'dwell' (יָשַׁב and the rest) is another sense altogether and is not looked for here.
others.title: Other words translated “life”, “living”, “alive”

h3117.note: יוֹם means day; the Berean prints “long life” for “length of days” (1 Kgs 3:11; 2 Chr 1:11; Job 12:12; Ps 91:16). It is a different word from חַי, and the page does not make the two one.

g2226.note: ζῷον, “living creature”, is a different word from the Hebrew חַי that the Berean also prints “living creatures” in Ezek 1:5 and 10:15; the four living creatures of Revelation 4 and 5 and those of Ezekiel are set side by side in the lists, and the page does not say the words, or the figures, are one.

_check: 16-verse sample against the Berean text (2026-10-25): 13 of 16 showed their row's label outright, 3 failed and were fixed. Luke 2:36 (the Berean prints 'had been married for seven years' for the Greek 'having lived with a husband seven years': out of 'The years one lived', by not_verses); Prov 29:24 ('hates his own soul') and Ezek 14:14 ('could deliver only themselves') were in 'A life laid down, lost, saved, sought, spared or loved' by the rule on the verb's object, but the Berean prints no 'life' there: out by not_verses. Also found by reading the picks against the text: Song 4:15 and Gen 26:19 print 'fresh water' for the Hebrew 'living water' (left out of the water row); Gen 5:3-30 and 11:12-24 print 'was 90 years old' for 'lived 90 years' (the row's label now says both); Isa 53:10 and Ps 49:8 print 'soul' (left out of the ransom row); Gen 45:27 prints 'revived' of Jacob's spirit (left out). Wrong turns kept: a rule on the word beside the noun for the oath 'as the LORD lives' took 10 verses of 'living creature' (נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה, Gen 1:20-24, 9:10-16) and missed 25 that the clauses split, so the row is by hand; a rule on 'day' or 'year' beside the word for 'the days of his life' found none (the phrase is split across parts), and 'any day in the verse' took 'today' (Deut 30:15), so that row is by hand too; the first sense rule counted English 'live' as 'dwell' in the 'other words' (יָשַׁב, 38 verses), which is another sense and is now excluded.

Still over 25, and the other fixes in '_review_2026_10_25' are held for the editor.

rows.label: The breath of life; the Spirit of life
rows.note: In Gen 2:7 (“the breath of life”), Gen 7:22 (“the breath of life in its nostrils”) and Job 12:10 (“the breath of all mankind”) the word is breath, and the page does not say it is the Spirit. Rom 8:2 (“the law of the Spirit of life”), Rom 8:6 (“the mind of the Spirit is life and peace”) and John 6:63 (“The Spirit gives life”) name the Spirit, and the Holy Spirit door is for those.

rows.label: The tree of life
A fountain, water, bread, light “of life”; and things called “living”
rows.note: “Of life” (חַיִּים, ζωή) and “living” (חַי, ζῶν) are different words, and the page does not make them one.

rows.label: The book of life; “recorded among the living”
rows.note: Ps 69:28 asks that the wicked be “blotted out of the Book of Life” and Rev 3:5 says “I will never blot out his name from the Book of Life”; Rev 13:8 and 17:8 speak of names “written ... from the foundation of the world in the Book of Life”. Where Christian traditions part on whether a name once written can be removed, and on what “from the foundation of the world” says of who is written, the page takes no side.

rows.label: Life set beside death
The life is in the blood
rows.note: Where the Berean prints “lifeblood” (Gen 9:4, 9:5) the Hebrew word is נֶפֶשׁ, here in its sense of “life”. Lev 17:11 goes on to say what the blood is given for on the altar; the blood and sacrifice cards read that verse in full, and the page takes no side here on what the blood does.

rows.label: Living creatures, every living thing
rows.note: The same Hebrew word is the living creatures of the sea and the earth (Gen 1) and the four “living creatures” of Ezekiel's vision (Ezek 1:5; 10:15).

rows.label: The living God; He who lives forever
rows._why: by hand, as the divine persons are: each verse says the living God or Him who lives forever; the Aramaic verses (Dan 4:34, 6:20, 6:26) are the Aramaic חַי, not the Hebrew word. Ps 18:46 and 2 Sam 22:47 (“The LORD lives, and blessed be my Rock!”) moved here 2026-10-25 from the oaths row (rulings sheet); the Hebrew words the page shows under Ps 18:46 belong to the neighbouring verse because of the Hebrew numbering.

rows.label: An oath by a life: “As surely as the LORD lives”, “as surely as I live”, “as surely as you live”, “as surely as Pharaoh lives”
rows.note: Amos 8:14 has those who swear by the guilt of Samaria say “As surely as your god lives, O Dan”, an oath by another god; Hos 4:15 says “do not journey to Gilgal, do not go up to Beth-aven, and do not swear on oath, ‘As surely as the LORD lives!’”.
rows._why: by hand: a rule on the phrase next to the word found 51 of these and 10 that were not oaths (Gen 1:20-24, 9:10-16, Lev 11:46: 'living creature'); the list is every verse where the Berean prints 'as surely as ... lives' or 'as surely as I live', read in the text. Ps 18:46 and 2 Sam 22:47 say 'The LORD lives, and blessed be my Rock!', which is a confession and not an oath; moved 2026-10-25 (rulings sheet) to 'The living God; He who lives forever'. Jer 38:16, 1 Kgs 1:29 and 2 Sam 4:9 add 'who has redeemed my life from all distress'.

rows.label: Alive, and the living: “still alive”, “taken alive”, “the living child”, “the land of the living”, “the living and the dead”, “as long as he lives”
The path of life; what leads to life or is life: wisdom, instruction, the fear of the LORD, righteousness
rows.note: Prov 8:35 (“whoever finds me finds life”) is the voice of wisdom in Prov 8; readers differ on whom that voice is, and the wisdom card reads the chapter. Here the verse is listed as written.

rows.label: Eternal life, said as had or given now: “has eternal life”, “you have eternal life”, “I give them eternal life”, “passed from death to life”
rows.note: Set beside the next two rows as the text has them. Where Christian traditions part on whether eternal life is a present possession, a gift still to come, or both, the page takes no side. John 3:15-16, 5:40, 6:40 and 20:31 (“may have”, “shall have”) are not placed in any of these three but in the row “Having life, eternal life”: whether “have” there is now or later is the question.

rows.label: Eternal life, said as still to come: “will inherit”, “enter life”, “in the age to come”, “in hope of”, “will reap”, “appointed for”, “the resurrection of life”
rows.note: Matt 25:46 sets eternal life beside eternal punishment; what that punishment is, readers part on, and the judgment card reads it. Acts 13:48 (“all who were appointed for eternal life believed”) is set among these as written; readers differ on what “appointed” says (God's choice, or those disposed to believe), and the page takes no side. Where Christian traditions part on whether eternal life is now or to come, the page takes no side. The verses that say “may have”, “shall not perish but have” and “shall have” are in the row “Having life, eternal life”.

rows.label: Now and later in the same verse: “has eternal life, and I will raise him up at the last day”; “in this age ... in the age to come”
rows.note: Set beside the two rows above. Where Christian traditions part on whether eternal life is now, to come, or both, the page takes no side; these are the verses that name both in one sentence. The verses that say “may have”, “shall not perish but have” and “shall have” are in the row “Having life, eternal life”.

rows.label: Having life, eternal life: “may have eternal life”, “shall not perish but have eternal life”, “to have life”, “you may have life in His name”
rows.note: Set beside the three rows above. These verses say “may have”, “shall not perish but have” and “shall have”, and whether that “have” is now or to come is the question; where Christian traditions part on whether eternal life is a present possession, a gift still to come, or both, the page takes no side.

rows.label: Christ and life: “I am the life”, “the resurrection and the life”, “the Author of life”, “Christ, who is your life”, “newness of life”, “life in His Son”
rows.note: John 6:53 (“unless you eat the flesh and drink the blood of the Son of Man, you have no life in you”) is read by Christian traditions as the Eucharist (the Lord's Supper), as faith in Christ, or as both; the page takes no side and shows the words as written, beside 6:35, 6:51 and 6:54.
rows._why: by hand (divine persons by hand): each verse names Jesus, Christ or the Son, or is Jesus' own 'I' and 'Me' (John 6:35, 11:25, 14:6). John 1:4 ('In Him was life') and 1 John 1:1-2 ('the Word of life', 'the eternal life that was with the Father') say 'Him' and 'the Word' and are left in 'Every other use' with a note.

rows.label: The days of life, the years of life, a lifetime, a long life
rows._why: by hand: a rule on 'day' or 'year' beside the word found none in the clauses (the phrase is split), and a rule on any 'day' in the verse took 'today' (Deut 30:15). The list is every verse where the Berean prints days, years, length, lifetime or a long life of a person's life, read in the text.

rows.label: The present life: how short it is; “Is not life more than food?”, “the pleasures of this life”, “the pride of life”, “this life alone”; and what one has to live on: “all she had to live on”, “all her money”, “his property”, “earthly possessions”
rows.note: The last six verses (Mark 12:44; Luke 8:43; 15:12; 15:30; 21:4; 1 John 3:17) use the Greek βίος in its sense of the means of living, which the Berean prints “all she had to live on”, “all her money”, “property”, “your wealth” and “earthly possessions”. That is a different sense from the length or the span of a life, listed here beside it, and the page does not make the two one.
rows._why: merged 2026-10-25 from two rows, 'The present life' and 'Livelihood' (panel B, as the way to bring the hub toward 15-25 without losing a verse; no seat on panel A objected). The Greek βίος is the means of living; the Berean prints 'all she had to live on' (Mark 12:44), 'all her money' (Luke 8:43), 'property' (Luke 15:12) and 'earthly possessions' (1 John 3:17). βίος in its other sense, the span or manner of life, was already in this row (Luke 8:14; 1 John 2:16).

rows.label: Weary of life: “I am weary of my life”, “I despise my own life”, “I hated life”, “better for me to die than to live”
rows._why: hard verses stay: the text records the wish and does not answer it in the same verse.

rows.label: A life laid down, lost, saved, sought, spared or loved

not_verses.Prov.29.24: the Berean prints 'hates his own soul'; the verse does not show 'life'
not_verses.Ezek.14.14: the Berean prints 'could deliver only themselves'; the verse does not show 'life'

rows.label: A life for a life: “life for life”, “a ransom for his life”, “atonement for your lives”, “to give His life as a ransom for many”, “lays down His life”
rows.note: The law asks a life for a life (Exod 21:23; Lev 24:18; Deut 19:21), refuses a ransom for a murderer's life (Num 35:31) and takes a ransom for each life in the census (Exod 30:12). Matt 20:28 and Mark 10:45 say the Son of Man came “to give His life as a ransom for many”, and John 10:11-18 that He lays down His life “of My own accord”. Where Christian traditions part on what the giving of His life does (a ransom paid, a penalty borne in place of others, a victory, an example, a covering), the page takes no side; the sacrifice, atonement and blood cards read these verses further. Jewish readers of the rabbinic period take Exod 21:23-25 (“a life for a life”) as payment of compensation, and the page takes no side.

rows.label: Phrases with “life”: “the promise: eternal life”, “the crown of life”, “the word of life”, “the full message of this new life”, “the gracious gift of life”, “the life of God”
Every other use

not_verses.1Kgs.3.11: the Berean prints 'long life' for the Hebrew word for 'days' (rulings sheet 2026-10-25): it stays only in the list of other words, under יוֹם
not_verses.2Chr.1.11: the Berean prints 'long life' for the Hebrew word for 'days' (rulings sheet 2026-10-25): it stays only in the list of other words, under יוֹם

rows.note: Among them John 1:4 (“In Him was life, and that life was the light of men”) and 1 John 1:1-2 (“the Word of life”, “the eternal life that was with the Father”), which say “Him” and “the Word”; readers take them of Christ from the passage around them (John 1:1, 1:14), and the page lists them as written. Rom 5:18 (“justification and life for all men”) is here as well: readers part on what “all men” takes in, and the page takes no side.

rows.label: God makes alive, revives, gives life: “I put to death and I bring to life”; “revive me”, “give me life”, “He will revive us”; “made alive with Christ”; “the Spirit gives life”
rows.note: The Greek ζῳοποιέω is said of the dead raised (Rom 4:17; 8:11; 1 Cor 15:22) and of the living made alive (Eph 2:5; Col 2:13; John 6:63). Where readers part on “all” in 1 Cor 15:22 (“in Christ all will be made alive”), and on whether Eph 2:5 and Col 2:13 speak of a new life now or only of the resurrection, the page takes no side. The Old Testament verses (Deut 32:39; 1 Sam 2:6; Ps 119; Ps 85:6; Isa 57:15) say the LORD brings to life and revives, in the same Hebrew verb חָיָה that the Greek Old Testament renders by ζῳοποιέω and ζάω; the page lists them together as the text has them and does not read the New Testament's “made alive” back into them. Hos 6:2 (“After two days He will revive us; on the third day He will raise us up”) is Israel's word about the LORD; readers take it of Israel's restoration, of the resurrection, or of both, and the page lists it as written and takes no side.
rows._why: by hand (divine persons by hand): each verse names God, the LORD, the Spirit, the Son or Christ. Merged 2026-10-25 from two rows, 'God makes alive' and 'Revive' (panel B: the same Hebrew verb with the same agent, split only by the Berean's English; no seat on panel A objected). Gal 3:21 (“a law that could impart life”) says what a law cannot do, not who gives it, and stays under 'Every other use'; 1 Cor 15:36 is a seed. 2 Kgs 5:7 is the king of Israel's question ('Am I God, killing and giving life?'), kept as a verse that names God as the one who gives life.

rows.label: Live by the commandments: “the man who does these things will live by them”, “Do this and you will live”, “live by every word”
rows.note: In Lev 18:5, Deut 4:1, 5:33, 8:1 and 30:16 the commandments are given that Israel may live. Paul quotes Lev 18:5 in Gal 3:12, just after Hab 2:4 in 3:11, and in Rom 10:5. Set beside the next row, as Gal 3:11-12 sets them. Where Christian traditions part on how living by the commandments and living by faith stand to each other (the law as a way of life, as a guide, as a schoolmaster to Christ, as ended), the page takes no side.

rows.label: Live by faith: “the righteous will live by faith”
rows.note: Set beside the row above. The Berean prints Hab 2:4 as “the righteous will live by faith” (the Hebrew word is faithfulness, or steadfastness), and the New Testament verses quote it as “by faith”; Heb 10:38 reads “My righteous one will live by faith”. The page takes no side on how the two rows relate.

rows.label: “Look and live”, “seek Me and live”, “turn and live”, “repent and live”
The dead live again: “will live”, “came to life”, “was dead and has come to life”, “alive”
rows.note: Ezek 37 is the valley of dry bones, which the chapter itself interprets (37:11-14: “these bones are the whole house of Israel”); readers take it of Israel's return, of the resurrection, or of both, and the page takes no side. Rev 20:4-5 says of those who reigned with Christ “they came to life” and of the rest that they “did not come back to life until the thousand years were complete”; readers part on whether that is a resurrection of the body, of the soul, or a figure, and on the thousand years, and the page takes no side. Job 14:14 is a question (“When a man dies, will he live again?”) and is kept as one. Rev 13:14 speaks of the beast “that had been wounded by the sword and yet had lived” (the same Greek verb, ἔζησεν, as in Rev 2:8), and the page says no more. Luke 15:24 and 15:32 are a father's words of his son in a parable (“was dead and is alive again”).

rows.label: To live to God, to righteousness, for the Lord, with Christ, by the Spirit: “because I live, you also will live”
The years one lived: “lived 140 years”, “was 90 years old”

not_verses.Luke.2.36: the Berean prints 'had been married for seven years'; the Greek is 'having lived with a husband seven years', and the verse does not show 'lived'
not_verses.Rev.20.5: the thousand years are the time before the rest 'came back to life': it is in the row of the dead who live again
not_verses.2Kgs.8.1: the seven years are a famine decreed; the verb is Elisha 'restored to life' the woman's son
not_verses.Hab.3.2: 'revive them in these years' is a plea to the LORD: it is in the row 'Revive'

rows._why: a rule: the verb 'live' with a count of years in the verse. Where the Hebrew is 'Enosh lived 90 years' the Berean prints 'When Enosh was 90 years old' (Gen 5:3-30; 11:12-24): the years of a life, as the label says.

rows.label: Every other use
rows.note: Verses with the word “living” are listed in the noun rows. Among them 'live' and 'let live' in the narratives (Gen 12:12; 20:7; 42:2; 45:7; 47:19; 50:20; Exod 1:17; Josh 6:25), Jer 27:17 and 38:20 (“serve the king of Babylon and live”; “obey ... and you will live”), Deut 30:6 (“so that you may live”), Heb 7:25 (“He always lives to intercede”) and 1 Cor 15:36 (the seed that is not made alive unless it dies).
